subject: Embeddings onboarding — Wave 0 runbook & fallback strategy
messages:
From: Katie Lopez <katie.lopez@atlas-retail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Iqbal <samir.iqbal@atlas-retail.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Embeddings kickoff — Scope & constraints

Thanks for the sync today, Mina. Quick recap from Atlas Retail:
- We have ~40M product descriptions (title + short blurb).
- Live search must support rerank for top-10 results within 150ms P95.
- Our compliance team needs retention policy (30 days for query logs, vectors stored indefinitely).

Primary asks:
1) What's the minimal Wave 0 scope so we can launch a low-risk pilot behind a feature flag?
2) How do you recommend handling index backfill without affecting production search latency?

Appreciate any outline you can share for owners and timelines.

— Katie
Director, Search & Discovery
Atlas Retail

--
Attachments: sample_export.csv (referenced), requirements_summary.docx (referenced)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embeddings kickoff — Scope & constraints

Thanks Katie — looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Grace (implementation PM). High-level proposal for Wave 0:

Wave 0 (low-risk pilot) — objectives:
- Surface embeddings-based rerank for a subset of 5 product categories (~1.2M docs).
- No customer-visible schema changes; behind feature flag and routed at service layer.
- Smoke test user cohorts only (non-critical traffic).

Index/backfill approach (recommended):
- Incremental shard-level backfill: start with cold shards for category-specific partitions to avoid hotspotting.
- Use prefix caching + KV warmup for popular SKUs to keep P95 within target.
- If backfill throughput risks latency, route live queries to a read-fallback ranker (existing BM25) until shard completes.

Rerank eval plan:
- Marissa will coordinate a 1,000-query sample (diversified by category & intent).
- Metrics: nDCG@10, MRR@5, and online click-lift (A/B).
- Acceptance gate: nDCG improvement >= 8% on blind sample and no >1% regression in latency-sensitive bucket.

I've attached a first-draft Wave 0 runbook and a small eval sample. Please review and flag anything missing.

Next steps:
- Marissa: create mutual action plan + timeline (ETA Wed).
- Grace: confirm backfill tooling (ETA Tue) and recommended vector DB config.
- Katie/Samir: confirm priority categories for Wave 0 by EOD Tue.

Best,
Mina
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: wave0-runbook.md (text/markdown), rerank-eval-sample.jsonl (application/jsonl)

Subject: Re: Embeddings kickoff — Scope & constraints

Quick update on the mutual action plan draft attached to the runbook:
- Week 0 (Prep): data contract, category list, and access to current search logs (owned by Atlas).
- Week 1–2 (Wave 0 index build): partitioned backfill (owner: Grace), vector DB schema locked to sharded collection per category.
- Week 3 (Eval & canary): run rerank evals offline; then 5% live canary off-peak.
- Week 4 (Roll): 25% traffic if canary metrics pass, otherwise rollback.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Backfill increases search database CPU. Mitigation: throttle backfill and use temporary burst capacity on Dedicated pool for build windows.
- Risk: Vector DB schema incompatibilities. Mitigation: use compatibility matrix (attached) and a small read-replica for canary.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Katie: confirm top 5 pilot categories — Tue EOD.
- Grace: share estimated backfill duration and shard sizing — Wed noon.
- Ben Carter: provide prebuilt client connector for chosen vector DB (cc'd).

I'll sync with Ben on the connector tests and prepare the eval harness.

Cheers,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Embeddings kickoff — Scope & constraints

Thanks all — short technical clarifications from the implementation side:

Vector DB choice and config notes:
- For Wave 0 we recommend Milvus-compatible schema on our Dedicated offering (lower ops overhead) but we can support an Atlas-managed Pinecone if Atlas prefers. See attached matrix.
- Sharding: category-level collections (roughly 200–300k docs per shard for even distribution).
- Index type: HNSW with M=16, efConstruction tuned for build speed; efSearch tuned during canary.

Backfill strategy detail:
- Phase A: dry-run on subset (10k docs) to validate tokenization and vector norms.
- Phase B: parallelized backfill using worker pool limited to 60% of standard DB IO to preserve search latency.
- Tombstone handling: we will preserve deletion flags and apply TTL only at the vector DB layer if Atlas confirms retention policy.

Operational fallback (on latency spike):
1) Auto-route traffic for flagged categories to BM25 ranker.
2) Pause backfill workers for most-impacted shards.
3) Escalate to Redwood on-call (Ben) for connector issues.

I'll provide an estimated backfill cadence after I run a shard-sizing test tonight.

— Grace
Implementation PM
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Embeddings kickoff — Wave 0 runbook & fallback strategy

Hi Katie & Samir — following up with a short checklist and test plan from the connector/ops side.

Connector & Ops checklist:
- I pushed a prebuilt connector to your sandbox cluster (endpoint sent in separate secure note).
- Please run the dry-run (Grace's Phase A) and share logs to the shared Drive link. Expected result: no tokenization drift and vector lengths within 0.5% of Redwood's sample.
- Smoke tests (to run during canary):
  * 500-query latency sweep (record P50/P95/P99).
  * 1,000-query rerank quality test using Marissa's sample.

Rollback checklist (if canary fails):
- Automatic rollback to BM25 (feature flag off).
- Revert any connector config changes pushed during the canary.
- Run postmortem with timeline and action items.

Proposed timeline (dates tentative):
- Dry-run & shard-sizing: Thu night (Grace).
- Backfill for Wave 0 partitions: Fri–Mon (throttled).
- Canary: Tue morning (5% traffic), decision by Tue EOD.

I'll be on standby for the canary window and will join the decision call.

Best,
Ben Carter
Platform Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference
